title: Compact evidence shepherding & inbound schema proposal for vuln pipelines
content:
Purpose:
This working proposal defines a compact, schema-first approach for collecting, deduplicating, and exporting vulnerability evidence from multiple scanner sources into our SIEM and ticketing systems. It pairs an inbound payload shape with an evidence shepherding flow that minimizes storage duplication and preserves auditable trails for RBAC v2 and compliance reviews.

Context & problem statement: 
- We ingest outputs from heterogeneous scanners (Trivy, Snyk, Dependabot, internal binary scanners). Each has different IDs, severity taxonomies, and attachment formats (JSON, SARIF, HTML).
- Current pipeline creates many duplicate evidence blobs (same file hash attached to separate findings), inconsistent field mappings to audit logs, and noisy SIEM entries that make triage slower.
- Audit reviewers and customers request per-finding provenance (who saw what, when evidence was attached) and immutable links to verification artifacts. RBAC v2 must be able to grant limited evidence-view access without exposing full ticket content.

Goals:
1) Define an inbound canonical payload for vulnerability findings that all adapters must emit.
2) Introduce an "evidence handle" (content-addressed ID) to avoid duplicate storage.
3) Provide a SIEM export mapping that preserves provenance and minimal PII while enabling detection rules.
4) Add RBAC v2 controls for evidence ingestion, de-dup access, and audit trail visibility.
5) Create actionable SLAs for patching and evidence closure, with automated enforcement hooks.

Proposed inbound payload (compact):
- finding_id: scanner-native id (string)
- canonical_key: generated key used across systems (string) e.g., canonical:{scanner}:{normalized-path}:{cve or fingerprint}
- title: short description (string)
- severity: normalized severity (critical/high/medium/low/info) (string)
- severity_source: original label (string)
- first_seen: ISO timestamp (string)
- last_seen: ISO timestamp (string)
- asset_id: internal asset identifier (string)
- package: package or component name (string)
- version: package version (string)
- cve: CVE identifier or null (string)
- fingerprint: deterministic fingerprint of the finding payload (sha256 hex) (string)
- evidence_handles: list of content-addressed handles (list of strings)
- evidence_manifest: list of metadata objects is disallowed in compact payloads; adapters should only submit handles and a small metadata string inlined in the handle registry.
- scanner: scanner name (string)
- scanner_link: link to raw scanner output (string)
- suggested_remediation: short remediation text (string)
- confidence: low/medium/high (string)
- tags: comma-delimited short tags (string)
- ttl: suggested lifecycle TTL for transient findings (e.g., 90d) (string)

Note: Because the agents.md schema requires flat values, we recommend adapters emit the above as flattened JSON; the ingest function will validate and upsert into the canonical findings store.

Evidence handle pattern and registry: 
- An evidence handle = eh:sha256:{hex}:metaref where metaref is a short stable label (e.g., build-1234-binary) to help humans. Store the actual object once indexed by sha256 to avoid duplicates.
- Ingest flow: adapter uploads raw evidence to evidence-bucket (s3 or gs) with content-md5 and content-type, gets back a handle, and then attaches the handle to findings via the inbound payload.
- Registry fields (kept in the evidence-store, not in each payload): content_type, size_bytes, object_path, uploader_id, upload_time, original_filename, scanner_ref. These are retrieved by authorized roles only.

Dedup & fingerprinting rules: 
- Primary dedup key is fingerprint. If fingerprint missing, compute deterministic fingerprint over normalized fields: package|version|path|cve|normalized-description.
- When duplicate fingerprints occur, merge findings preserving earliest first_seen and union of evidence_handles.

SIEM export mapping (streaming):
- For each finding we emit a compact SIEM event with the following fields (flattened):
  - event_type: vuln_finding
  - canonical_key
  - severity
  - asset_id
  - cve
  - fingerprint
  - evidence_handle_count
  - first_seen
  - last_seen
  - remediation_owner (redacted email to role@redwood.com for SIEM)
  - ingestion_cluster_region
  - scanner
  - tags (comma-delimited)
- Avoid sending full file contents or raw scanner HTML to SIEM. Instead, send evidence_handle(s) and a retrieval token for authorized systems.

RBAC v2 controls (high level):
- Roles proposed: scanner-adapter (ingest-only), evidence-reader (can resolve handles to metadata), triage-engineer (view + transition findings), remediation-owner (view + attach remediation artifacts), security-auditor (view-only across teams), approver (can close P0/P1 findings).
- Scopes: evidence:read:asset:{asset_id}, evidence:attach, finding:transition, finding:export:siem.
- Enforcement: token-based access with short-lived certs issued by control-plane; evidence retrieval endpoints validate scope and return only metadata for SIEM-bound tokens.

Patch SLA & remediation tracking proposal: 
- SLA tiers (recommended):
  - P0 (critical exploit path / exposed): remediation target 24 hours to a verified patch or mitigation; verification within 48 hours.
  - P1 (high, easy exploit): remediation target 7 days; verification within 14 days.
  - P2 (medium): remediation target 30 days.
  - P3 (low/info): triage within 90 days.
- Automated enforcement: findings are tagged with sla_tier and a deadline timestamp. An orchestration job runs every 6 hours to escalate approaching deadlines: send Slack, create or update Jira ticket, and mark for exec escalation if overdue by >2x deadline.
- Closure requires: remediation steps documented, evidence handles for patched artifacts, and a verification run (scanner pass) appended. Verification success must be an inbound payload that references the original canonical_key and includes scanner:verification-run with pass=true.

Remediation ticketing and audit trail: 
- Ticket model: Jira ticket must include canonical_key in the title and the primary fingerprint as a custom field to enable downstream automation.
- Evidence attachments should never be embedded as ticket file blobs; instead tickets contain evidence_handle(s) and retrieval tokens limited by RBAC. This keeps tickets lightweight and centralizes evidence retention policy.
- Audit log schema for actions (flat event string to be stored in audit index):
  - audit_event_type (string) e.g., evidence_upload, finding_merge, ticket_link, sla_escalation
  - actor_id (string)
  - actor_role (string)
  - target_canonical_key (string)
  - evidence_handle (string) optional
  - timestamp (ISO string)
  - result (string) success|failure|partial
  - change_summary (short text)

Operational runbook (short):
1) Adapter onboarding: provide a small shim that outputs the compact payload. Validate with test vectors (included in repo).
2) Evidence ingestion: adapters upload to evidence-bucket, call evidence-registry, then emit finding payload.
3) Triage: security triage UI resolves merged findings, assigns remediation_owner.
4) Remediation: remediation-owner attaches evidence_handle(s) for patched artifacts and sets verification run; orchestration picks up verification and closes per SLA.
5) Audit: all state transitions emit audit_event entries stored for 2 years by default.

Open questions & next steps:
- Do we require all adapters to compute a fingerprint, or will ingest compute it when missing? (tradeoff: trust vs. consistent determinism)
- Metadata exposure: confirm allowed fields in SIEM for GDPR-sensitive environments (we recommend role-level redaction by default).
- RBAC v2 policy syntax: map proposed scopes to the control-plane policy DSL and prototype a policy for scanner-adapter and evidence-reader.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Priya: prototype ingest validator and fingerprint library (ETA 2 weeks).
- Ethan: SIEM export prototype with redaction rules (ETA 3 weeks).
- Zara: draft RBAC v2 policy examples and run a tabletop with SRE (ETA 1 week).
- Marco: create onboarding checklist and test vectors in github.com/redwood-inference/vuln-ingest (ETA 5 days).

Appendix: example flattened inbound JSON (single-line example for adapters to copy/paste):
{"finding_id":"trivy-12345","canonical_key":"canonical:trivy:/srv/app/api:pkg@1.2.3:CVE-2025-9999","title":"Unsafe deserialization in pkg","severity":"high","severity_source":"HIGH","first_seen":"2026-11-18T14:22:00Z","last_seen":"2026-11-18T14:22:00Z","asset_id":"aws:ec2:i-0abcd1234","package":"pkg","version":"1.2.3","cve":"CVE-2025-9999","fingerprint":"3f8e...deadbeef","evidence_handles":"eh:sha256:abcdef...:build-1234","scanner":"trivy","scanner_link":"https://scanner.internal/r/12345","suggested_remediation":"upgrade to 1.2.4 or apply patch X","confidence":"high","tags":"web,production","ttl":"90d"}

Notes: this is a working doc intended to guide engineering and compliance alignment. Feedback welcome — please add inline comments or reply in #sec-vuln with your notes.
